uncited: *   **Input:** 3D Gaussian splat parameters (mean $\mathbf{m}$ in camera space, covariance $\Sigma$), camera intrinsic parameters (focal length $f$), and equirectangular image dimensions $(W, H)$.
*   **Output:** Axis-aligned bounding box $(p_{x,\min}, p_{x,\max}, p_{y,\min}, p_{y,\max})$ in equirectangular pixel coordinates.
*   **Tangent Space Basis:** Vectors $\hat{\mathbf{t}}$ (tangent), $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ (bitangent), $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ (normal) in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
*   **Tangent Box:** Rectangle defined by $t_{x,\min}, t_{x,\max}, t_{y,\min}, t_{y,\max}$ in tangent space.
*   **Camera Space Box:** Derived from tangent box via transformation.
For a splat with mean $\mathbf{m}$ in camera space, determine the reference vector $\mathbf{r}_{\text{ref}}$ to avoid pole singularities.
Compute the normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}} = \mathbf{m} / \|\mathbf{m}\|$.
Compute the tangent $\hat{\mathbf{t}} = \text{normalize}(\mathbf{r}_{\text{ref}} \times \hat{\mathbf{n}})$.
Construct the transformation matrix $M$ from camera space to tangent space.
The columns of $M$ are $\hat{\mathbf{t}}, \hat{\mathbf{b}}, \hat{\mathbf{n}}$.
Map the tangent box corners back to camera space.
A point in tangent space is $\mathbf{t} = (t_x, t_y, 1)^T$.
Convert camera space coordinates to spherical angles (longitude $\phi$, latitude $\lambda$) or directly to equirectangular coordinates $(p_x, p_y)$.
The equirectangular coordinates are proportional to $\phi$ and $\lambda$.
Due to the non-linear nature of $\text{atan2}$ and $\text{asin}$, the bounding box in equirectangular space is not simply the projection of the tangent box corners.
Directly using $\text{atan2}$ is problematic due to discontinuity at the pole cut.
Compute the range of longitude $\phi$ covered by the box.
Check if the projected bounding box covers the north or south pole.
*   If it covers a pole: Set $p_{x,\min} = 0$ and $p_{x,\max} = W$ (full image width).
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per splat for the bounding box calculation, involving constant number of matrix-vector multiplications and trigonometric functions.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ per splat, storing only the basis vectors and box coordinates.
It addresses the limitations of standard 3DGS rasterization, which assumes a local affine approximation that fails under non-linear spherical projections.
The approach builds on the tangent space formulation used in HTGS [HFW*25] and extends it to the equirectangular domain.
